latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_target_revalidation_2026_11_17: Surface target binding now revalidates the source-bound candidate, camera and viewport at click time. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_typed_witness_2026_11_17: Added an unconnected source-evaluated typed-point witness for standalone NURBS surfaces. Its cancellable world-space projection applies the full occurrence placement to positions and derivatives, and validates trim topology and UV membership before returning a witness. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_typed_worker_2026_11_17: Connected an initial cancellable, admitted tracked-document witness worker to typed coordinates and Between subpoints on standalone surfaces. A source witness within tolerance authorizes the original explicit coordinate; the pending job checks occurrence, prompt revision, Between state, CPlane, add-on token and draft before acceptance, and changed keyboard or pointer input cancels it. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_typed_brep_2026_11_17: Added an initial OCCT adapter that obtains a world-space witness on an individual trimmed face, including edges, instead of measuring distance to a solid. Typed surface workers capture canonical BRep sources, honor the selected face or iterate polysurface faces with cancellation between calls, and reject a result after a document-tolerance change. NativeBrep conversion remains open. Face-order mapping, nonuniform placement, native allocations, cancellation inside OCCT, closest-point correctness and UI lifecycle are uncompiled and untested; the native adapter requires rebuild, SDK and runtime validation in P07.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_typed_native_2026_11_17: Extended the typed witness worker to capture the selected NativeBrep payload, convert it with bounded admission, compare its face count with the selected source receipt and check each converted trimmed face. The worker now waits cooperatively for the shared surface-snap slot, so a just-canceled hover worker does not immediately reject typed input. Native conversion allocations, face-index correspondence, nonuniform transforms, close/cancel races, contention and stale-result guards require the deferred native build and runtime checks; these changes are uncompiled and untested.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.surface_typed_trim_boundary_2026_11_17: Typed standalone-surface verification now also searches the actual UV trim segments, evaluates candidate points on the source surface and accepts only a world-space witness within tolerance. This covers supported trim boundary and seam points without assuming an ambiguous UV classification is inside. The bounded sampled search can miss a valid point, and topology validation, nonuniform placement, work limits, cancellation and source residuals remain uncompiled and untested.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.sdk_incomplete_query_2026_11_17: The synchronous SDK query now refuses eligible source-edge and general-intersection work that only the viewport workers can perform, instead of returning an incomplete candidate ranking as an authoritative hit or miss. The conservative guard can reject distant sources; asynchronous SDK parity still needs an implementation. Documented this limitation in the SDK README. Uncompiled and untested.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.smarttrack_source_worker_2026_11_17: Extended the intersection worker request with up to four captured SmartTrack guides and scheduled source extraction even when Intersection is off. The worker bounds each transient guide against each source curve's world-space control hull, evaluates guide/curve intersections with the existing source solver, and ranks them as source-bound SmartTrack candidates after ordinary snaps. Guide changes invalidate worker results. NURBS, extracted BRep/NativeBrep edges, trim edges, cancellation, pair budgets, numerical solver completeness, occlusion and deferred-click behavior are uncompiled and untested; the general solver can miss intersections and some transformed curves remain unsupported.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.line_nurbs_hulls_2026_11_17: Added a bounded, cancellable positive-weight NURBS control-hull subdivision for general line/curve intersections after the existing analytic line and quadratic paths. It retains possible tangencies without requiring a sign change and checks a source-evaluated midpoint against the finite line in document tolerance; possible overlap and budget/parameter failures are explicit refusals. This also feeds SmartTrack guide intersections. The interval bounds, floating-point margins, parameterization, deduplication, overlap handling, performance and existing analytic precedence are uncompiled and untested; do not claim global numerical certification.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.nurbs_pair_hulls_2026_11_17: Added bounded paired positive-weight control-hull subdivision for NURBS/NURBS source intersections, including tangent contacts, with source-evaluated tolerance witnesses, cancellation, explicit equal-curve overlap refusal and bounded work. Its numerical margins, self-intersection interval interaction, close/overlapping curves, deduplication, transformed sources, memory and runtime cost remain uncompiled and untested; other curve-pair families still use the existing numeric search.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.affine_arc_mid_2026_11_17: Added world-space half-length midpoint evaluation for nonuniformly transformed circular arcs using bounded, cancellable Simpson refinement and bisection. Circle-preserving transforms retain the direct midpoint angle. This is a numerical estimate, not a certified integration error bound; transformed instances, high eccentricity, tolerance, performance and cancellation need P07 validation. The calculation is still performed in the synchronous scene query and should be moved to the revision-keyed worker path before claiming responsiveness. Uncompiled and untested.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.affine_arc_worker_2026_11_17: Deferred circular midpoint candidates in the interactive viewport query and extended the admitted source/view workers to retain circular curve parts, including polycurve segments. The SDK's synchronous scene query still evaluates the midpoint inline. Verify cache invalidation, one-shot Mid, circle-only and mixed polycurve occurrences, admission and worker cancellation in P07. This supersedes the previous note about interactive midpoint computation remaining synchronous; changes remain uncompiled and untested.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.snap_regressions_prepared_2026_11_17: Prepared focused existing-suite regressions for cubic tangent intersections and source residuals, placed-surface projection, transformed-arc midpoint/deferred candidate parity, and face-only BRep witnesses excluding a solid interior. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.self_intersection_subdivision_2026_11_17: Replaced the fixed eight-way self-intersection partition with bounded source-hull subdivision until each positive-weight NURBS piece has a monotone control projection on every active knot span, then compares distinct pieces. This remains uncompiled and untested: validate monotonicity assumptions, periodic/reversed seams, loops close to joints, source parameter remapping, budget accounting, and tangent/overlap cases in P07. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.affine_arc_near_2026_11_17: Replaced the single-bracket sampled Near search on placed circles/arcs with bounded screen-box subdivision using source trigonometric extrema, camera depth clipping and a 0.05-pixel stopping criterion. Numerical enclosure, clipping, degenerate views, cancellation and performance remain uncompiled and untested; this is not a formal floating-point certificate.
latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.affine_arc_perpendicular_2026_11_17: Replaced sign-change-only perpendicular searches for transformed circles/arcs with bounded subdivision of the normal equation using a derivative bound, tolerance-checked source witnesses and cancellation. latest_snaps_implementation_2026_11_17.nested_elevator_prompt_2026_11_17: Avoided duplicate outer-prompt and one-shot completion handling when Elevator supplies a nested Between point, and prepared a regression checking the second subprompt and the single midpoint delivered to Line. minimum_window.why: User decisions: smallest supported device 1366x768; window not shrinkable below 1280x720 logical; right-dock threshold delegated to the agent ('sao cho hop ly la duoc').

decisions.window_minimum: startup::effective_min_size: per axis max(800x400 floor, min(1280x720, monitor_logical - (16,80))); unknown monitor -> 1280x720. Builder gets the floor 800x400; MatrixApp::show sends ViewportCommand::MinInnerSize on frame 0 and on change. AppConfig.min_window nominal 1280x720 (start below it refused).
decisions.high_dpi_conflict: 1366x768 at 125%/150% is 1093x614 / 911x512 logical; a hard 1280x720 cannot fit, so the minimum is capped to the usable area: 1366x768@100% -> 1280x688, @125% -> 1076.8x534.4, @150% -> 894.7x432. Work area is ESTIMATED (egui/winit do not expose it; Win32 would need unsafe/FFI). Reserve includes the title bar (one constant SHELL_RESERVE_PT; taskbar-only is a user choice).
decisions.planner_floor: PLAN_FLOOR_WINDOW 800x400 replaces 560x286 (320x286 without rail); rail-independent. Behaviour below the floor unchanged (WindowTooSmall, Layout: error, last good plan). NotEnoughRoom and LeftRailShrunk unreachable, variants kept.
decisions.right_dock_threshold: NARROW_WINDOW_WIDTH 900 -> 1200 logical points. Viewport width (W-602)/2 is 299 pt at 1200 vs 156.5 pt at the old 915.

RESOLVED AND GREEN: the harness expectation was stale and is corrected. The scenario now forces the window-readback path with a 300x40 rectangle; the app clamps it to [28,49,300,120] (FLOAT_MIN_HEIGHT) and says 'Display was moved back inside the window'; one frame later the REAL window reports its own 132 px height, above the minimum and inside the work area, which the readback legitimately accepts. The harness asserts on the forced clamp and the message (float_after_force.2/3, message_after_force) instead of the frame-later state. Full harness: 7/7 PASS.

Window harness: 7/7 PASS (verified twice; one earlier 'float-drop exit -1' was a race with a concurrent cargo build, not a code regression — run alone it passes). The Object Info label still has no window photo. Findings for the next attempt: (1) OM9_UI_AUDIT_PANELS is validated against PANEL_AUDIT_SCENARIOS in ui.rs, so a new scenario needs its name added there (this was the real cause of the three timeouts); (2) record_panel_checks DOES fill left_order, work_area, floating and drag_in_progress from live state, so a receipt whose checks lack those fields did not come from the arm we added — verify the dispatch actually takes it (log audit.panel_checks.len()) before trusting the run.

The scenario passes on its own (3 consecutive runs) and in a full run was once killed by the OS (exit -1, no receipt) — a harness-level transient already seen with float-drop; a one-retry in tools/validate_m01_l3_003_panels.py is the next small fix. Two real causes found on the way: the scenario name had to be added to PANEL_AUDIT_SCENARIOS (ui.rs) and the dispatch arm needed `return` (without it the default drag script ran too).

items.title: 13-febe-matrix-transform-toolbar-bridges
items.scope: OM9-L2-04-01, 20 M03-owned L3 of 41 catalogued Transform rows: 39 rows run a verified command body; the remaining 2 stay visible and disabled with the reason their own contracts record (Solid Points ON needs sub-object grips, Make Down Facing is BLOCKED_OWNER).
items.why: Direct user request 2026-10-26: check whether the L2-04-01 Transform toolbar bridge code exists, implement what is missing and update the milestone dashboard.
items.summary: The audit found the artwork and wiring but no command layer: menu_catalog::TRANSFORM, MainMenu.ini [Menu10] and ui/chrome.rs already render the 41 rows and icons.rs already answers every feature id, yet Controller::availability had no Transform answer, so every row rendered disabled and a click did nothing. New crates/om9-app/src/transform_menu.rs is the 41-row catalog (L3 id, Matrix label, authored script, feature id, state, disabled reason) and new crates/om9-app/src/session/transform.rs owns the command bodies: Scale 3D/2D/1D/Non-Uniform, Scale By Plane, Orient 2/3 Points, Rotate3D, Array Polar/Linear/Array, Set Points, Project To C-Plane and Remap to C-Plane. Every point resolves through the captured CPlane with coords::parse_input + resolve_with_base, every scalar is validated at its own prompt, and one finished command is one transaction: Mutation::Placement in place, Mutation::Insert for array copies. The transform arithmetic is never re-implemented here - om9_core::gumball supplies scaling_along/rotation_about/rectangular_array/polar_array and om9_core::transform_session supplies the align solve. The menu click and the typed name reach the same begin_transform through dispatch_geometry and from_alias. The follow-up parity audit (2026-10-26, round 2) gave every catalog row its authored MainMenu.ini/icons.rs key, fixed the Array Curve on Surface artwork that was bound to Array Along Curve, and pinned the two rows that have no authored artwork. The third pass (2026-10-27) implemented the two curve rows that the earlier audit had wrongly reported as having no owner service: Orient Perpendicular to Curve snaps the picked point to the nearest station by bisection on the signed tangent projection and aligns each object's plane normal with the curve tangent, and Array Along Curve measures equal arc-length stations with curve_ops::arc_length/length_between. Both take their path curve from the selection (exactly one selected curve is the path, every other selected object is transformed along it) because the shell has no mid-command object pick. The same pass fixed Controller::commit_transform_mutations to apply one step per object when a row hands in one step per target, which is what makes Project To C-Plane drop objects from different heights onto the plane. The fourth pass (2026-10-27, reference-frame rows) enabled six rows whose owner services already existed in om9-core but were never called: Orient on Surface projects the picked point with curve_surface_ops::closest_point_on_surface and stands the object on surface_kernel::normal; Orient on Curve snaps to the nearest station and turns the object's X axis onto the curve tangent; Symmetry commits an affine reflection of the placement, so every geometry kind mirrors without a geometry-specific mirror routine; Array Along Surface fills the evaluated grid of the selected surface; Array Curve on Surface samples equal arc-length stations and projects each one onto the surface; Stretch is the one-direction scale from gumball::scaling_along. All six live in the new crates/om9-app/src/session/transform/rows.rs behind the same begin_transform/dispatch path, so the menu click and the typed name still reach one body, and every row is one transaction. The two rows that remain without an owner service are Solid Points ON (no sub-object control-point selection) and Make Down Facing (UNRESOLVED_BLOCK_ENABLE). The fifth pass (2026-10-27, deformers) added the kernel deformer layer crates/om9-core/src/deform.rs (bend, taper, twist, shear, maelstrom, soft move) and enabled six rows; the sixth pass added the three flow owners (flow along curve, flow along surface, splop) in the same module. A nonlinear map writes geometry because it cannot live in a placement, a shear is the affine case that keeps a line a line, and a solid is refused with a typed error instead of being deformed on its display mesh. The seventh pass (2026-10-27) added MoveUVN: deform::move_uvn offsets a surface's control net along the U tangent, the V tangent and the normal at every pole's Greville parameter, reusing surface_kernel::greville_parameter and the exact derivatives, and refusing any non-surface selection. The eighth pass (2026-10-27) implemented the cage family against its M08 owner OM9-L3-04-08-005: om9-core cage.rs gained box cages, an exact Newton parameter inversion, the displacement field and the cage mesh, the document model gained the om9.cage extension slot, and Create Cage / Cage Edit / ReleaseFromCage run as three commands with one Undo entry each. The ninth pass (2026-10-27) implemented the Smart Flow family against its M08 owners OM9-L3-04-05-002/-003/-005/-006: deform::rigid_flow, deform::pulldown_from_target and the om9.flow link slot (base, target, rigid, revision, ACTIVE/BROKEN) now back SmartFlow, SmartFlowRigid, SmartFlowBreak and SmartFlowPullDownCurves.

notes: 2026-11-06 P1 optional topology cache registration: experimental proof cache is now registered with the shared optional-memory reclamation coordinator; it atomically retires at most one unpinned proof per callback and reports only reservations actually released. An Upload-pressure fixture verifies retry after eviction, pinned-proof survival and unchanged document/Undo/scene; a published scene also pins its proof. App topology-owner 29 passed/2 ignored; one-root GPU test passed. Proof creation is still test-only, no large-model/desktop evidence, and document/Undo mesh separation and v5 remain incomplete.

2026-11-06 P1 pressure retry diagnosis: after retiring the idle proof the retained-inventory diagnostic showed 66,792 bytes headroom; a 65,537-byte request leaves 1,255 bytes while document validation scratch is estimated at 5,319 bytes. This supports validation scratch as the reason for the observed refusal, not a lost proof reservation. The adjusted fixture leaves the scratch and verifies automatic reservation retry succeeds after eviction while target/pinned proofs and document/Undo/scene remain unchanged. This result is fixture-specific; global proof-cache reclamation and general admission/headroom reporting remain open.

2026-11-06 P1 experimental remesh pressure: reservation retries after retiring one idle non-target proof at a time, preserving pinned and target proofs. Test verifies actual CPU reservation decreases and document/Undo/scene remain unchanged; retry works after external pressure is released. Under the saturated fixture, automatic retry still returned Budget(bytes) despite releasing 1,256 bytes, so success solely from eviction is unproven and admission/headroom discrepancy needs investigation. This path is remesh-only, not registered in global optional-cache reclamation; app topology-owner 29 passed/2 ignored.

2026-11-06 P1 proof rebind after unrelated edit: experimental Controller retains only proofs whose document session, object generation and geometry revision remain unchanged; a later remesh revalidates full source/display under an admitted scratch reservation before rebinding the current context. Active workers block rebind; deleted/changed sources are refused. Two-root fixture remeshes after adding an unrelated point; app topology-owner 28 passed/2 ignored, kernel topology 6 passed/3 probes ignored and one-root GPU passed. Normal commands still do not create proofs, cache eviction under pressure is not implemented, and v5/document mesh separation remain open.

2026-11-06 P1 multi-root controller prototype: controller stores multiple in-process topology proofs with a separately reserved owner per additional entry, selects a root explicitly and keeps other proofs across verified display-only publications; document changes clear them. A box+sphere fixture remeshes both independently, checks the other root's buffer remains, verifies face picking IDs and invalidates proofs after edit. App topology-owner 27 passed/2 ignored and one-root GPU test passed. Proof construction remains test-only; UI/real model multi-root integration, multi-root GPU/performance, independent document/Undo display ownership and v5 remain incomplete.

2026-11-06 P1 source record OCCT count gate: the experimental kernel helper validates the record then compares its face/edge/vertex counts against independently parsed OCCT source. An app fixture adds a face UUID and recomputes a valid record hash; decoding succeeds but OCCT count check refuses it. The valid box and kernel source-inspection tests pass. Equal counts cannot establish UUID/subshape correspondence, native allocation remains unbounded, and no codec or UI uses this gate yet.

2026-11-06 P1 canonical source OCCT inspection: an OCCT 8.0.1 adapter reads and BRepCheck-validates source and counts faces/edges/vertices without display tessellation. Kernel fixtures box/sphere and invalid source pass; an app test validates capture -> reserved canonical record -> source inspection for a box. C++ is limited to OCCT parsing/checking; Rust owns record and reservation. Counts are snapshot-local and do not prove UUID correspondence or global accuracy; native allocations are not bounded and node limits are checked after parsing. The API is not connected to codec/UI; P1 remains open.

2026-11-06 P1 source/topology record integrity: the experimental record now hashes source fingerprint together with ordered UUIDs and face-edge adjacency; altered IDs are refused. Core B-rep 23, archive unit 6 and v4 codec 8 pass. This is accidental-corruption detection, not authentication or proof that IDs map to OCCT subshapes; it does not enable remeshing or v5 migration.

2026-11-06 P1 standalone canonical record reservation: decode now requires a physically sampled, pending CpuCache reservation from the matching account and returns a guard retaining the record charge; cancellation, under-budget and foreign-account requests release it. A peer-account test verifies charge lifetime. Archive unit 6 and related v4 integration 20 pass. The input remains separately owned and preflight may conservatively double-charge it; allocator bound and integration into the project codec/document lifecycle, OCCT validity and UUID provenance remain open.

2026-11-06 P1 standalone canonical-record admission: om9-archive now offers a separate source/topology record decoder that invokes existing streaming JSON preflight and an admission callback before typed deserialization, then checks actual record capacities, integrity and UUID/adjacency. Refusal, duplicate keys and corruption tests pass; archive unit 5 and v4-related integration 20 pass. This is not yet a project codec or v5 migration: allocator upper bounds and lifetime reservation integration still need proof, as do OCCT validity and persistent topology provenance.

2026-11-06 P1 source-only wire record: core now exposes a borrowed canonical B-rep source/topology view from a tracked lease and an independent untrusted record with digest, ID, adjacency and scratch validation, rejecting unknown record/topology fields. Tests serialize after display release and reject corruption/admission refusal; core B-rep 23 and related v4 archive 20 pass. Decoder preflight before deserialization, OCCT validity, native topology provenance, NativeBrep, hydration and integration into a real v5 codec remain open; v4 format is unchanged.

2026-11-06 P1 v5 dependency review: om9-archive depends on om9-core, and the current decoder deserializes Document directly with mandatory Brep.display. A genuinely source-only v5 requires a core source/topology representation and an explicit hydration/cache boundary before codec migration; changing the version header alone would be incorrect. Legacy v4 UUID provenance remains unverified; preserve its existing cache or refuse unsafe remesh rather than guessing source index mapping.

2026-11-06 P1 scene owner across document replacement: the reserved replacement path now binds its candidate scene-buffer lease before publishing. Tests retain independent old/new buffers through replacement and drop, and retain an incremental buffer through Undo; incremental memory 9/9 and replacement-budget 9/9 pass. This validates those fixtures, not every external account or consumer. Owner chains may conservatively over-retain; multi-root controller, document/Undo display eviction and v5 remain open.
